notes.meaning: David speaks honestly to the Lord, insisting that he is not puffed up with pride inside, nor does he look down on others. He refuses to chase after human glory, power, or hidden mysteries that belong only to God. Instead of forcing his own ambitions, he chooses to stay humble within the boundaries God gives him.

Instead of remaining restless and demanding, David has quieted his inner cravings. A nursing baby cries for milk, but an older weaned child rests peacefully against its mother just to be near her. In the same way, David has learned to be satisfied with God Himself rather than fretting over what he wants to receive.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early and medieval teachers saw the weaned child as a picture of spiritual growth, where a believer moves past the basic milk of the faith into the stronger discipline of mature life in the church.

notes.meaning: David turns from his own life to urge the whole nation of Israel to share that same peaceful posture. Rather than scheming or rushing ahead of God, the people are told to place all their confidence in the Lord. This quiet, patient trust is meant to guide them both right now and into the future.
